a11y.statement.intro: Jokerless aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA on the web, and the matching Apple and Android guidance in the apps. We are working towards that aim and do not yet claim to meet it in full.
a11y.statement.limits.board: The game board is still being made fully accessible. Some games cannot yet be played from start to finish with only a screen reader or only a keyboard.
a11y.statement.limits.heading: Known limitations
a11y.statement.limits.legal: The terms and the privacy notice are available in fewer languages than the app itself.
a11y.statement.limits.native: The iOS and Android apps have not yet been reviewed by people who use assistive technology every day.
a11y.statement.limits.translations: Some newer accessibility wording may appear in English until it is translated.
a11y.statement.report.body: If something does not work for you with a screen reader, a keyboard, large text or any other assistive technology, please tell us what you were trying to do and which device, browser or app version you were using (Account menu → About shows the version).
a11y.statement.report.heading: Report a problem
a11y.statement.report.issue: Or open an issue in the public tracker:
a11y.statement.reviewed: This statement was last reviewed in October 2026.
a11y.statement.supported.heading: What works today
a11y.statement.supported.keyboard: Keyboard: every control outside a game can be reached with Tab and used with Enter or Space. The arrow keys move between choices in a group, and Escape closes menus and tooltips.
a11y.statement.supported.screenReaders: Screen readers (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA and others): the screens outside a game have named buttons, headings, labelled form fields and spoken error messages.
a11y.statement.supported.settings: Settings → Accessibility: screen reader announcements, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts, a four-colour deck, high contrast, card size, reduced motion, and a confirmation before moves that end the hand.
a11y.statement.supported.text: Text size: the screens outside a game follow your browser zoom and your device text size, and their text wraps rather than being cut off.
a11y.statement.supported.tooltips: Tooltips: icon buttons and badges explain themselves on hover, on keyboard focus and on a long press, and screen readers read the same words.
a11y.statement.title: Accessibility

blackjack.rules.aces: An ace counts as eleven while that fits, and as one when it does not.
blackjack.rules.blackjack: An ace with a ten-value card, on the first two cards, is a blackjack.
blackjack.rules.bustedOut: A seat that can no longer cover the minimum of {n} sits out the rest of the match.
blackjack.rules.dealerDraws: The dealer draws to seventeen and then stands.
blackjack.rules.dealerPeeks: Showing an ace or a ten, the dealer checks for blackjack before anybody plays.
blackjack.rules.double: On your first two cards you may double your stake and take exactly one more card.
blackjack.rules.doubleAfterSplit: A hand that came out of a split may be doubled too.
blackjack.rules.faceUp: Player cards are dealt face up; the dealer keeps one card down until everyone has played.
blackjack.rules.goal: Beat the dealer without going over twenty-one. Going over loses at once, whatever the dealer does afterwards.
blackjack.rules.hitStand: Draw as many cards as you like, or stand on what you have.
blackjack.rules.hitsSoft17: The dealer draws to a seventeen made with an ace.
blackjack.rules.insurance: Against a dealer ace you may insure for half your stake; it pays 2:1 if the dealer has blackjack.
blackjack.rules.leave: You may get up whenever you like. With cards in front of you, you play the round out first. Your chips go with you and are your result.
blackjack.rules.leaveAway: A player whose connection has dropped for {minutes} minutes leaves the table with their chips.
blackjack.rules.leaveAwayNever: A player whose connection drops is sat out until they return.
blackjack.rules.mostChipsWins: Whoever holds the most chips at the end wins the match.
blackjack.rules.noDoubleAfterSplit: A hand that came out of a split may not be doubled.
blackjack.rules.noInsurance: Insurance is not offered at this table.
blackjack.rules.noSplit: Pairs are not split at this table.
blackjack.rules.noSurrender: Hands cannot be surrendered at this table.
blackjack.rules.oneStakePerRound: One stake per round — once it is up it cannot be changed.
blackjack.rules.roundOrder: A round goes in order: stakes up, cards dealt, insurance if the dealer shows an ace, then each seat plays its hand in turn.
blackjack.rules.split: Two cards of the same value may be split into hands of their own, each with its own stake — up to {n} times, for {hands} hands in all.
blackjack.rules.splitAces: Split aces take one card each and then stand, and twenty-one made that way is not a blackjack.
blackjack.rules.stack: Every seat sits down with {n} chips.
blackjack.rules.stakeFromStack: You can only stake chips you actually hold.
blackjack.rules.standsSoft17: The dealer stands on a seventeen made with an ace.
blackjack.rules.surrender: You may give up your first hand for half its stake, once the dealer has checked for blackjack.

canasta.rules.blackThreesGoOut: A black three blocks the discard pile and is worth {n} points. Three or more of them may be melded straight from your hand, never with a wild card among them, and only as part of going out: once they are down you may keep at most one card, to discard.
canasta.rules.blackThreesNeverMeld: A black three is never melded. It blocks the discard pile when discarded, and costs {n} points if it is still in your hand when the deal ends.
canasta.rules.canasta: A canasta is a meld of {n} or more cards of the same rank.
canasta.rules.canastaCloses: A canasta of {n} is complete and takes no more cards.
canasta.rules.deck: Played with {value} cards — {decks} decks plus jokers.
canasta.rules.dirtySequences: A meld can also be a sequence: three to seven cards of one suit in a row. Wild cards may stand in for missing cards, at most two and never more than half as many as the natural cards. Seven with a wild in them is a dirty samba, worth {n}.
canasta.rules.drawCount: You draw {n} cards at the start of your turn.
canasta.rules.end: The deal keeps being redealt until one side passes {n} points — then the match is over.
canasta.rules.goOutKeepsACard: You must always be able to finish your turn, so never meld away your whole hand unless it is the move that goes out.
canasta.rules.goal: Play in partnerships; the first side to reach {n} points wins the match.
canasta.rules.goingOutBonus: Going out is worth {n} points on its own — {concealed} if your side does it in a single turn, with nothing melded before that.
canasta.rules.goingOutBonusFlat: Going out is worth {n} points on its own.
canasta.rules.layOffAfterOpening: Until your side has made its initial meld it may lay off only natural cards, and only onto melds it laid this turn. Those count toward the minimum.
canasta.rules.meldFloorBands: Your first meld must reach a point minimum that rises with your score: {negative} below zero, {low} up to {lowUpTo}, {mid} up to {midUpTo}, {high} beyond that.
canasta.rules.meldFloorBandsFive: Your first meld must reach a point minimum that rises with your score: {negative} below zero, {low} up to {lowUpTo}, {mid} up to {midUpTo}, {high} up to {highUpTo}, {top} beyond that.
canasta.rules.meldShape: A meld is {n} or more cards of the same rank.
canasta.rules.meldsAreShared: Melds belong to the partnership: either partner may extend them, and neither side may touch the other's.
canasta.rules.meldsPerRankUnlimited: Your side may have several melds of the same rank.
canasta.rules.oneCanastaToGoOut: One completed canasta is enough for your side to go out.
canasta.rules.oneMeldPerRank: Your side keeps one meld of each rank — more cards of that rank are laid off onto it.
canasta.rules.pileAlwaysFrozen: The discard pile is frozen all deal: to take it you must match its top card with two natural cards from your hand.
canasta.rules.pileBlocked: A black three on top blocks the pile — nobody may take it until the three is buried — and one left in your hand costs {n}.
canasta.rules.pileFrozenByWild: A wild card buried in the pile freezes it against everyone: taking it then costs two natural cards of the top card's rank, out of your own hand.
canasta.rules.pileNoMeldCapture: A meld already on the table cannot take the discard pile: to take it you must match its top card with two cards from your own hand.
canasta.rules.pileOntoMeld: If your side already has an unfinished meld of the top card's rank, you can take the whole discard pile to add that card to it — no matching pair in your hand is needed.
canasta.rules.pileTopCard: The discard pile can only be taken by a move that uses its top card straight away.
canasta.rules.poach: On your turn, once your side has opened, you may swap a natural card from your hand for the wild card it stands for in any meld on the table, and keep the wild.
canasta.rules.rearrange: On your turn, once your side has opened, you may move cards between your side's own melds, as long as every meld stays legal. A canasta broken this way is no longer a canasta.
canasta.rules.redThrees: A red three in your hand is shown immediately and scores as a bonus — unless your side never completes a canasta, when it counts against you instead.
canasta.rules.samba: A sequence of seven cards is a samba, worth {n} points.
canasta.rules.sequences: A meld can also be a sequence: three or more cards of the same suit in a row, never with a wild card among them.
canasta.rules.stockOut: Once the stock is empty, play goes on only while the player on turn can take the discard pile and still finish the turn — when they cannot, the deal ends.
canasta.rules.topOnlyCapture: Whenever you could take the discard pile, you may take only its top card instead, melded the same way, and leave the rest of the pile.
canasta.rules.turn: A turn is one move into your hand — draw from the stock, or take the whole discard pile — then any melds you want to lay, then one card discarded.
canasta.rules.turnDiscard: The discard is what ends a turn, so you always need a card to spare for it.
canasta.rules.twoCanastasToGoOut: Your side needs two completed canastas before it may go out.
canasta.rules.wildLimit: A meld may hold at most {wilds} wild cards, and never fewer than {naturals} natural ones.
canasta.rules.wildMeld: Once your side has opened it may lay one meld of 2s, with jokers beside them at most half as many as the 2s. Seven cards is a canasta: {n} if all 2s, {mixed} with jokers.
canasta.rules.wildRatio: A meld needs {n} natural cards for every wild one, and never more than {wilds} wilds in all.

ginrummy.prompt.yourTurnDiscard: Discard — or knock, if you can
ginrummy.remedy.discardToEndTurn: Discard one card to end your turn.
ginrummy.remedy.drawElsewhere: That pile is empty — draw from the other one.
ginrummy.remedy.drawFirst: Draw a card first — from the stock or the discard pile.
ginrummy.remedy.finishLayoff: Nothing more of yours fits — finish laying off.
ginrummy.remedy.getDeadwoodDown: You can knock once your deadwood is {n} or less.
ginrummy.remedy.stockDrawForced: You both passed that card — draw from the stock.
ginrummy.remedy.takeOrPassUpcard: Take the upcard, or pass it.
ginrummy.rules.aceLow: The ace is always low — there is no run from Queen through Ace.
ginrummy.rules.bigGinBonus: Eleven cards melding with no discard at all is big gin, worth a further {n} points.
ginrummy.rules.box: Each hand you won is worth {n} points at the end of the match.
ginrummy.rules.deadHandDescription: If the stock runs down to its last two cards and nobody has knocked, the hand is dead — nobody scores, and the same dealer deals again.
ginrummy.rules.drawDiscard: On your turn, draw one card — from the stock or the discard pile — then discard one.
ginrummy.rules.gameBonus: Winning the match is worth a further {n} points.
ginrummy.rules.gin: Zero deadwood is gin — the best possible knock.
ginrummy.rules.ginBonus: Gin scores your opponent's whole hand, plus {n}.
ginrummy.rules.knockLimit: You may knock once your deadwood is {n} or less.
ginrummy.rules.knockOnDiscard: A knock replaces your discard, so it can only happen at the end of your turn.
ginrummy.rules.layoffDescription: After a knock that is not gin, your opponent may lay their own deadwood onto your melds before the hands are compared.
ginrummy.rules.oklahoma: This hand's knock limit is set by the value of the upcard.
ginrummy.rules.setsAndRuns: A meld is a set of three or four cards of one rank, or a run of three or more in one suit.
ginrummy.rules.shutout: The game bonus doubles to {n} if the loser never scored a single point.
ginrummy.rules.target: First to pass {n} points after a hand ends wins the match.
ginrummy.rules.undercut: If your opponent's deadwood is no higher than yours, they undercut you: they score the difference, plus {n}.
ginrummy.rules.upcard: One more card is turned face up to start the discard pile.
ginrummy.rules.upcardDance: Before the first draw the non-dealer may take the upcard, then the dealer may; if both pass, the non-dealer must draw from the stock.

holdem.remedy.callAllInOrFold: Your stack will not get above the bet — call {n} all in, or fold.
holdem.remedy.callOrFold: There is {n} to call — call, raise, or fold.
holdem.remedy.checkOrRaise: Nothing is owed — check, or raise.
holdem.remedy.discardOrStand: It is the draw — pick one to {n} cards to swap, or stand pat.
holdem.remedy.nameAnAmount: Say how much to raise to, between {min} and {max}.
holdem.remedy.nothingToShow: You were not dealt into this hand — wait for the next one.
holdem.remedy.raiseAtMost: Raise to at most {n} — that is your whole stack.
holdem.remedy.raiseAtMostPot: Raise to at most {n} — that is the size of the pot.
holdem.remedy.waitForNextHand: You are out of this hand — wait for the next deal.
holdem.rules.allIn: You can never put in more than your stack, and going all in is always allowed — even for less than a full raise.
holdem.rules.blinds: The small blind is {sb} and the big blind is {bb}, posted before the cards are dealt.
holdem.rules.cash.away: A player whose connection has dropped for {minutes} minutes leaves the table with their chips.
holdem.rules.cash.awayNever: A player whose connection drops is sat out until they return.
holdem.rules.cash.leave: At a cash table you may get up whenever you like. Your chips go with you and are your result.
holdem.rules.checkOrCall: You may check only when nothing is owed; otherwise call, raise or fold.
holdem.rules.draw.deal: Each player is dealt five cards face down. There is no board: your hand is the five cards you hold.
holdem.rules.draw.draw: In the draw, each player still in the hand, starting left of the dealer, throws away one to {n} cards and is dealt as many new ones — or stands pat and keeps all five. Players who are all in draw too.
holdem.rules.draw.public: Everyone is told how many cards each player drew, but never which ones.
holdem.rules.draw.streets: Betting happens in two rounds — one on the cards as dealt, and one after the draw.
holdem.rules.foldedOut: Once you fold you are out until the next hand is dealt.
holdem.rules.goal: Win chips by having the best hand at showdown, or by being the only player left in the hand.
holdem.rules.lastPlayerStanding: The match plays until one seat holds every chip.
holdem.rules.minRaise: A raise has to be at least as big as the last one.
holdem.rules.mostChipsWins: Whoever holds the most chips when play stops wins the match.
holdem.rules.noLimit: No-limit betting — any bet may be for any amount up to your whole stack.
holdem.rules.omaha.allIn: You can never put in more than your stack, or more than the pot allows. Going all in is allowed whenever your stack fits under that limit — even for less than a full raise.
holdem.rules.omaha.deal: Each player is dealt four cards face down.
holdem.rules.omaha.useTwo: Your hand must use exactly two of your four cards and exactly three from the board.
holdem.rules.potLimit: Pot-limit betting — a raise can be at most the size of the pot after you call.
holdem.rules.revealEveryone: At a showdown every hand that was called is turned face up.
holdem.rules.revealWinners: At a showdown only the winning hand is turned face up.
holdem.rules.showOnce: A hand can be shown only once.
holdem.rules.showYourOwn: You may always turn your own hand face up, until you agree to go on.
holdem.rules.showdown: Players still in the hand reveal their cards; the best five-card hand wins the pot.
holdem.rules.stopEveryHand: Play stops after every hand, so the cards can be seen.
holdem.rules.streets: Betting happens in four rounds — before the flop, and after the flop, turn and river are dealt.
holdem.rules.tournament: This is a tournament: it is played to the last chip, and nobody leaves with theirs. A player who is away is sat out, and their blinds are still posted.

klondike.remedy.playTheTable: Play the cards on the table.
klondike.remedy.turnEverythingUp: Turn up every card first; then the rest plays itself.
klondike.remedy.turnWasteOver: Turn the waste over to draw again.
klondike.rules.autoFinish: Once every card is face up, Finish plays the rest out for you.
klondike.rules.autoFlip: A face-down card left on top of a column turns up by itself.
klondike.rules.build: Columns build down in alternating colours: a red six on a black seven.
klondike.rules.deal: Seven columns are dealt of one to seven cards, only the top card of each face up. The other 24 cards are the stock.
klondike.rules.draw1: The stock turns one card at a time onto the waste.
klondike.rules.draw3: The stock turns three cards at a time onto the waste; only the top one can be played.
klondike.rules.foundation: The four foundations build up by suit, from ace to king.
klondike.rules.kingOnly: Only a king, or a run headed by one, can fill an empty column.
klondike.rules.lost: You can give up at any time; the game counts as lost.
klondike.rules.noAutoFinish: Every card is played out by hand, to the last one.
klondike.rules.noTakeBack: A card on a foundation stays there.
klondike.rules.redealsLimited: The waste may be turned over {n} times.
klondike.rules.redealsNone: The waste is never turned over: one pass through the stock.
klondike.rules.redealsUnlimited: The waste may be turned over as often as you like.
klondike.rules.runs: Any face-up run moves as one, from the card you pick up to the bottom of the column.
klondike.rules.scoreStandard: Waste to column 5, any card to a foundation 10, turning a card up 5, a card back off a foundation −15.
klondike.rules.scoreVegas: You start at −52 and every card on a foundation is worth 5.
klondike.rules.solo: One player against the deck. Nobody else moves at this table.
klondike.rules.stock: When the stock is empty, the waste can be turned back over to make a new stock.
klondike.rules.stuck: The game ends by itself when nothing is left that could change it, or after {n} moves in a row that got nowhere.
klondike.rules.takeBack: A card may come back down from a foundation onto a column.
klondike.rules.undo: Undo takes back a move, but never a card turned up or drawn.
klondike.rules.won: You win when all 52 cards are on the foundations.

lastcard.prompt.drawFour: {player} hit you with a Wild Draw Four. Take the four cards — or challenge it if you think it was a bluff.
lastcard.prompt.playDrawnOrKeep: You drew {card} — play it now, or keep it.
lastcard.prompt.stack: {n} cards are coming your way — stack a draw card on them, or take them.
lastcard.remedy.answerDrawFour: {player} played a Wild Draw Four — take the four cards or challenge it.
lastcard.remedy.followColourFirst: You still hold a {colour} card — play that, or draw.
lastcard.remedy.matchOrDraw: Play a {colour} card, or one that matches {card} — otherwise draw.
lastcard.remedy.nowPlay: You've called it — now play your card.
lastcard.remedy.playDrawnOrKeep: Play the card you drew ({card}), or keep it.
lastcard.remedy.playOrDraw: Play a card, or draw one.
lastcard.remedy.stackOrTake: Answer with a draw card of your own, or take the {n} cards.
lastcard.rules.call: Holding two cards, say “Last card!” before you play the second-to-last one.
lastcard.rules.catch: Forget, and the next player may catch you before they move: you draw two cards.
lastcard.rules.challenge: Hit by a Wild Draw Four, you may challenge it. A bluff makes its player draw the four instead; an honest card makes you draw six and miss your turn. Either way you see the hand it came from.
lastcard.rules.deck: A {value}-card pack in four colours — coral, teal, violet and amber — each numbered 0 to 9 with Skip, Reverse and Draw Two cards, plus Wilds and Wild Draw Fours.
lastcard.rules.drawTwo: Draw Two: the next player draws two cards and misses their turn.
lastcard.rules.end: The match ends the moment someone's hand is empty.
lastcard.rules.end.lowest: The match ends when someone's total reaches {target}, and the lowest total wins.
lastcard.rules.end.points: The match ends when someone's total reaches {target} points.
lastcard.rules.goal: Be the first to play every card in your hand.
lastcard.rules.goal.lowest: Keep your total low: after every deal you pay for the cards left in your hand. When someone reaches {target}, the lowest total wins.
lastcard.rules.goal.points: Be the first to reach {target} points. Each deal is won by whoever empties their hand first.
lastcard.rules.reverse: Reverse: play changes direction. With two players it works like a Skip.
lastcard.rules.scoring: Whoever goes out scores the cards left in everyone else's hands. First to {target} wins.
lastcard.rules.scoring.lowest: When someone goes out, every other player is charged the points left in their own hand. When a total reaches {target}, the lowest total wins.
lastcard.rules.sevens: Play a 7 and you swap hands with whoever holds the fewest cards.
lastcard.rules.skip: Skip: the next player misses their turn.
lastcard.rules.stacking.any: Stacking: answer a draw card with one of your own — a Draw Two on a Draw Two, a Wild Draw Four on either — and pass the whole stack on. Whoever can't, takes it all and misses their turn.
lastcard.rules.stacking.twos: Stacking: answer a Draw Two with a Draw Two of your own and pass the whole stack on. Whoever can't, takes it all and misses their turn.
lastcard.rules.turn.draw: If you don't play, draw one card. If it fits, you may play it straight away or keep it; either way your turn then ends.
lastcard.rules.turn.drawUntil: If you don't play, draw until a card you can play turns up — then play it or keep it. Either way your turn then ends.
lastcard.rules.turn.match: Play one card that matches the top card by colour, by number or by symbol — or play a Wild.
lastcard.rules.values: Number cards score their number; Skip, Reverse and Draw Two score 20; wilds score 50.
lastcard.rules.wild: Wild: goes on anything. Name the colour that continues.
lastcard.rules.wildDrawFour: Wild Draw Four: name the colour, and the next player draws four and misses their turn. Only allowed when you hold no card of the colour in play.
lastcard.rules.wildDrawFourBluff: Wild Draw Four: name the colour, and the next player draws four and misses their turn. It is only honest when you hold no card of the colour in play — but you may bluff.
lastcard.rules.zeros: Play a 0 and every hand passes to the next player in the direction of play.

marias.prompt.answer: {player} plays {game}. Say dobrá, or take it over with a higher game.
marias.prompt.flek: Double or announce what you dare, then say nothing more.
marias.prompt.hold: {player} bids {rung}. Say mám to hold it, or pass.
marias.prompt.keepSeven: Keep your seven of trumps for the last trick.
marias.prompt.talon: Lay two cards away to the talon.

marias.rules.bid.announce: The chooser picks up their 12 cards, announces a game and lays two away. They may not pass.
marias.rules.bid.flek: Each part can be doubled on its own: the side that did not announce it doubles first, then the sides take turns ({names}). The turn goes round until a full circle passes without a doubling.
marias.rules.bid.flekLimit: A part can be doubled at most {n} times.
marias.rules.bid.proti: A defender may announce sedma proti (they hold the 7 of trumps and will win the last trick with it) or sto proti (the defenders will reach a hundred).
marias.rules.bid.takeover: In turn, each other player says dobrá, or špatná and a higher game: betl over hra, sedma or sto; durch over any of those or over betl. They take the talon, lay two away and become the declarer. Nothing goes over durch.
marias.rules.deal.roles: The player left of the dealer chooses. They get 7 cards, then 5 more after naming trumps (12 in all); the others get 10 each. The chooser changes every deal.
marias.rules.deal.talon: The declarer lays two cards away to the talon. In hra, sedma and sto neither may be an eso or a 10. The talon counts as the declarer's.
marias.rules.deal.trump: The chooser names trumps by choosing one of their first seven cards.
marias.rules.deal.turns: Everything goes clockwise: choosing, answering, doubling and play.
marias.rules.deal.zLidu: Or z lidu: by taking a card unseen from the five they have not looked at.
marias.rules.deck: {value} German-suited cards: hearts (červené), bells (kule), acorns (žaludy) and leaves (zelené); 7, 8, 9, 10, spodek, svršek, král and eso.
marias.rules.four.deals: With four players, the match is rounded up to a multiple of four deals, so everyone sits out equally often.
marias.rules.four.sitOut: With four players, the dealer sits each deal out and neither pays nor is paid; the player on their left chooses.
marias.rules.game.betl: Betl: take no trick. No trumps.
marias.rules.game.durch: Durch: take every trick. No trumps.
marias.rules.game.dveSedmy: Dvě sedmy: name trumps and a helper suit, then win the trick before last with the helper suit's 7 and the last trick with the trump 7. Neither seven may be played early or be beaten, or the contract is lost.
marias.rules.game.hra: Hra: take more points than both defenders together, counting marriages.
marias.rules.game.sedma: Sedma: win the last trick with the 7 of trumps. Announced with hra or sto, and settled separately from it.
marias.rules.game.sto: Sto: reach {n} with card points and the first marriage announced. It replaces hra and may be announced with sedma.
marias.rules.goal: Each deal, one player (the declarer) plays a game alone against the other two. Win units from the others; after the last deal, the most units wins.
marias.rules.licit.auction: The dealer bids first against the player on the dealer's left (the forhont), naming a rung of the ladder or passing; the forhont holds it by saying mám, or passes. At equal rungs the forhont wins.
marias.rules.licit.bluff: Above plain sedma a contract need not match the cards; plain sedma needs the 7 of trumps.
marias.rules.licit.contract: The winner takes the talon and announces any contract at or above the rung won, with its trumps.
marias.rules.licit.deal: Everyone gets 10 cards; the other 2 lie face down as the talon until the auction is won.
marias.rules.licit.ladder: The ladder, low to high: sedma, sedma červená, sto, sto a sedma, sto červených, sto a sedma červených, betl, durch, dvě sedmy, dvě sedmy a sto, and both dvě sedmy with hearts as trumps. Červená means hearts are trumps.
marias.rules.licit.lead: The forhont leads to the first trick, whoever declares, except in betl and durch, where the declarer leads. Whoever wins a trick leads to the next.
marias.rules.licit.middle: When one of them passes, the third player takes their place: bidding against the forhont, or holding against the dealer.
marias.rules.licit.noProti: The defenders announce nothing of their own: no sedma or sto proti.
marias.rules.licit.nobody: If nobody bids, the forhont plays sedma.
marias.rules.licit.omyl: A declarer held to plain sedma may fold instead of playing (omyl), paying {n} to each defender.
marias.rules.order.plain: In betl and durch the order is eso, král, svršek, spodek, 10, 9, 8, 7.
marias.rules.order.trump: In hra, sedma and sto the order is eso, 10, král, svršek, spodek, 9, 8, 7.
marias.rules.play.earlyEnd: Betl ends at the declarer's first trick, and durch at their first trick lost.
marias.rules.play.follow: Follow suit if you can, and beat the best card of that suit in the trick if you can. Once the trick has been trumped, any card of the suit led will do.
marias.rules.play.lead: The declarer leads to the first trick. Whoever wins a trick leads to the next.
marias.rules.play.marriage: Play the svršek while holding the král of the same suit to announce a marriage: {plain}, or {trump} in trumps. No marriages in betl or durch.
marias.rules.play.openHand: In betl and durch the declarer lays their cards face up once the first trick has been played.
marias.rules.play.seven: Whoever announced a sedma keeps the 7 of trumps for the last trick unless no other card is legal.
marias.rules.play.trump: If you cannot follow, play a trump, and beat any trump already in the trick if you can. With neither, play anything.
